terms.label: GPU
terms.def: A processor with thousands of simple cores and its own memory, built to run the same small program on many pieces of data at once.

terms.label: Streaming multiprocessor / compute unit (SM / CU)
terms.def: A GPU building block (NVIDIA SM, AMD CU) that contains many of the small cores (lanes) and runs shader threads in lockstep groups.

terms.label: VRAM
terms.def: The GPU's own memory: very fast for the GPU, far away from the CPU.

terms.label: Command processor
terms.def: The GPU's front end: it reads command buffers from memory and hands the work they describe to the rest of the chip.

terms.label: Hardware engine
terms.def: An independent unit inside the GPU that executes one kind of work: graphics, compute, copy (DMA) or video.

terms.label: Driver (ICD)
terms.def: Vendor code that turns API calls into the GPU's own command format; the Vulkan loader documentation calls it an Installable Client Driver.

terms.label: Command buffer
terms.def: A recorded list of GPU commands, submitted to a queue as one unit.

terms.label: Queue
terms.def: A line of submitted command buffers for one hardware engine; submission order is the logical order that barriers and semaphores refer to, but by itself it orders nothing: work may overlap and finish out of order unless you synchronize it.

terms.label: OpenGL state machine
terms.def: OpenGL's model: one hidden global context of current state that every call reads and changes, validated and compiled by the driver on the fly.

terms.label: Explicit API
terms.def: An API where the application states everything up front (memory, synchronization, state) instead of the driver guessing.

terms.label: Vulkan object
terms.def: Anything the API creates and destroys explicitly: instances, devices, buffers, pipelines and so on.

terms.label: Handle
terms.def: An opaque value (VkInstance, VkDevice ...) that names an object living inside the loader or driver.

terms.label: Vulkan SDK
terms.def: The LunarG package of headers, loader, validation layers, shader compilers and tools (vulkaninfo, vkconfig) for developing Vulkan apps.

terms.label: ash
terms.def: Thin Rust bindings that expose the Vulkan C API one to one.

terms.label: Vulkan-Hpp
terms.def: Khronos' C++ bindings over the C API, with RAII wrappers (vk::raii) that destroy objects automatically.

terms.label: Vulkan loader
terms.def: The vulkan-1 library an app talks to: it finds the installed drivers and layers and routes every call to them.

terms.label: Layer
terms.def: A library inserted between the app and the driver that sees every call passing through (validation, profiling, capture).

terms.label: Extension
terms.def: An optional, named piece of API functionality that must be enabled when the instance or device is created.

terms.label: VkInstance
terms.def: The application's connection to the Vulkan loader: the root object everything else comes from.

terms.label: Validation layer
terms.def: The Khronos layer that checks every call against the specification's valid-usage rules and reports violations.

terms.label: VkDebugUtilsMessengerEXT
terms.def: An object that delivers layer and driver messages to a callback in our code.

terms.label: VkPhysicalDevice
terms.def: One GPU as the instance sees it: enumerated (never created) and used to query properties, features, limits and queue families.

terms.label: Features
terms.def: Optional capabilities a GPU may support; each must be enabled when the logical device is created before it can be used.

terms.label: Limits
terms.def: Numbers a GPU guarantees (largest image, required alignments ...), read from its properties.

terms.label: Queue family
terms.def: A group of queues with the same capabilities (graphics, compute, transfer ...), usually backed by one kind of hardware engine.

terms.label: VkDevice
terms.def: Our opened session with one GPU, with the chosen features and queues enabled; it creates almost every other object.

terms.label: VkQueue
terms.def: A handle to one queue of the device: the place where command buffers are submitted.

terms.label: Window system integration (WSI)
terms.def: The extensions that connect Vulkan to the operating system's windows: a portable surface extension, one per platform to create surfaces, and the swapchain extension; core Vulkan itself only renders into images.

terms.label: VkSurfaceKHR
terms.def: An OS window as Vulkan sees it: an instance-level object created from the native window handle, which a GPU's queue families can be asked to present to.

terms.label: Surface capabilities
terms.def: What the window system allows for one GPU and one surface: image count range, current and allowed sizes, transforms, alpha compositing and image usages.

terms.label: Presentation engine
terms.def: The platform's machinery that puts finished images on the display (on Windows the desktop compositor together with the display driver); it uses the swapchain's images (the swapchain owns them) and lends them to the application one at a time.

terms.label: VkSwapchainKHR
terms.def: A small ring of presentable images for one surface, created from the device through VK_KHR_swapchain: the application acquires an image, renders into it and presents it back.

terms.label: Swapchain image
terms.def: A VkImage created and owned by the swapchain: the application gets its handle with vkGetSwapchainImagesKHR and never creates or destroys it.

terms.label: Surface format
terms.def: A pixel format plus a color space that the window system can display; the format says how values are stored, the color space how the screen interprets them.

terms.label: Present mode
terms.def: The rule by which presented images replace each other on screen: FIFO (a queue drained once per vertical blank, always supported), MAILBOX, IMMEDIATE and others.

terms.label: VkImage
terms.def: A block of texels with a format, size, mip levels and array layers, usually arranged in memory in a way only the driver knows (optimal tiling): textures, depth buffers, render targets.

terms.label: VkImageView
terms.def: A way to look at an image: a view type, a format, a channel mapping and a range of aspects, mip levels and layers. Rendering and shaders use views, not images.

terms.label: Shader
terms.def: A small program the GPU runs for every vertex, pixel or work item; a stage of the pipeline that the application programs, built on the GPU's shader cores.

terms.label: Slang
terms.def: A shading language with HLSL-like syntax, hosted by Khronos and shipped with the Vulkan SDK; its compiler slangc emits SPIR-V for Vulkan.

terms.label: SPIR-V
terms.def: Khronos' binary intermediate language for shaders: a stream of 32-bit words that Vulkan accepts instead of source code; the driver compiles it further for its GPU.

terms.label: VkShaderModule
terms.def: SPIR-V code handed to the device; it may hold several entry points, and it is only needed until the pipelines that use it are created.

terms.label: Graphics pipeline
terms.def: The sequence of stages that turns vertices into pixels: input assembly, vertex shading, rasterization, fragment shading, tests and blending; some stages are programmable, the rest fixed-function.

terms.label: Fixed-function stage
terms.def: A pipeline stage that is not a shader but hardware with settings: input assembly, rasterization, depth and stencil tests, color blending.

terms.label: VkPipeline
terms.def: A graphics pipeline baked into one object: shader stages plus the settings of every fixed-function stage, compiled by the driver when it is created.

terms.label: Dynamic state
terms.def: A piece of pipeline state that is declared dynamic at pipeline creation and set with a vkCmdSet* command while recording, instead of being baked into the pipeline.

terms.label: VkDescriptorSetLayout
terms.def: The shape of a group of shader resources: binding numbers, resource types and the stages that see them. Pipeline layouts list set layouts, and every descriptor set is allocated with one.

terms.label: VkPipelineLayout
terms.def: The full list of resource slots a pipeline's shaders can see: its descriptor set layouts plus its push constant ranges. Every pipeline needs one, even an empty one.

terms.label: Dynamic rendering
terms.def: Rendering into attachments named while recording (vkCmdBeginRendering), with pipelines that state only the attachment formats; core since Vulkan 1.3, it replaces render pass and framebuffer objects for most uses.

terms.label: Attachment
terms.def: An image view that a rendering writes to (color, depth, stencil): the render target of a draw.

terms.label: Load and store operations
terms.def: What happens to an attachment's contents when a rendering begins (load, clear, don't care) and ends (store, don't care).

terms.label: VkRenderPass
terms.def: The Vulkan 1.0 way to describe attachments and subpasses up front, paired with a VkFramebuffer of image views; still valid, mostly replaced by dynamic rendering.

terms.label: VkCommandPool
terms.def: The memory that command buffers of one queue family are allocated from; destroying the pool frees all its command buffers.

terms.label: VkCommandBuffer
terms.def: The Vulkan object for a command buffer: allocated from a pool, recorded with vkCmd* calls between begin and end, submitted to a queue.

terms.label: Recording
terms.def: Writing commands into a command buffer on the CPU (vkCmd* calls between vkBeginCommandBuffer and vkEndCommandBuffer); nothing runs on the GPU until the buffer is submitted.

terms.label: Queue submission
terms.def: Handing recorded command buffers to a queue (vkQueueSubmit2), together with the semaphores to wait on and signal and an optional fence.

terms.label: VkFence
terms.def: A GPU-to-CPU signal: a submission signals it when its work completes, and the CPU waits on it with vkWaitForFences.

terms.label: VkSemaphore
terms.def: A GPU-side signal: a batch or the presentation engine (when an acquired image is free) signals it, and a batch or a present waits on it. For a binary semaphore the host is not involved; a timeline semaphore can also be waited on and signaled by the host.

terms.label: Image layout
terms.def: The arrangement of an image's memory for one kind of use (color attachment, presentation, sampling ...); an image is moved between layouts by a barrier.

terms.label: Pipeline barrier
terms.def: A command recorded into a command buffer (vkCmdPipelineBarrier2) that orders the commands before it in submission order against the commands after it: their work in the source stages completes, and their writes by the source accesses are made available and visible to the destination accesses, before the later work in the destination stages starts; an image barrier can also transition the image's layout.

terms.label: Frame loop
terms.def: The round trip of one frame: wait for the previous frame, acquire a swapchain image, record, submit, present.

terms.label: Execution dependency
terms.def: A guarantee that one set of operations happens-before another: the first set completes before the second set starts. Built on submission order, defined by a synchronization command (fence, semaphore, barrier) through its two synchronization scopes.

terms.label: Binary semaphore
terms.def: A VkSemaphore with two states: a signal sets it, and exactly one wait consumes the signal and unsets it again. The only kind of semaphore that acquire and present accept.

terms.label: Frames in flight
terms.def: Several frames being worked on at once: the CPU records frame N+1 while the GPU still renders frame N. Built on the frame loop with one set of per-frame resources (command buffer, fence, acquire semaphore) per frame in flight.

terms.label: Data hazard
terms.def: Two accesses to the same memory, at least one of them a write, with no dependency ordering them: read-after-write and write-after-write need a memory dependency, write-after-read only an execution dependency.

terms.label: Memory dependency
terms.def: An execution dependency that also includes availability and visibility operations, so that values written by the first set of operations can be read or overwritten by the second set; most synchronization commands define one.

terms.label: Availability and visibility
terms.def: The two halves of a memory dependency: availability makes the writes of the first access scope available to a memory domain (like flushing the writer's caches), visibility makes available values visible to the accesses of the second access scope (like invalidating the reader's caches).

terms.label: Pipeline stage mask
terms.def: The pipeline stages a synchronization scope covers: srcStageMask names the stages of earlier work that must complete, dstStageMask the stages of later work that must wait; a semaphore wait carries one too.

terms.label: Access mask
terms.def: The kinds of memory access an access scope covers: srcAccessMask the writes to make available, dstAccessMask the accesses to make them visible to; each access must belong to a stage of the matching stage mask.

terms.label: Layout transition
terms.def: The change of an image's layout inside an image memory barrier: a read and write of the image's memory that happens after the barrier's availability operations and before its visibility operations.

terms.label: Timeline semaphore
terms.def: A VkSemaphore built on a 64-bit counter that only grows: a signal sets it to a larger value, a wait (in a submission or on the host) lasts until it reaches a value. Core since Vulkan 1.2; one can replace a set of fences.

terms.label: Swapchain recreation
terms.def: Building a new swapchain when the old one no longer fits the window (a resize, OUT_OF_DATE, SUBOPTIMAL), handing the old one over as oldSwapchain and destroying it once nothing uses it.

terms.label: Retired swapchain (oldSwapchain)
terms.def: The swapchain passed as oldSwapchain when its replacement is created: it becomes retired, so no image can be acquired from it any more, images already acquired may still be presented, and the application still has to destroy it.

terms.label: Present fence
terms.def: A fence given to vkQueuePresentKHR (VK_KHR_swapchain_maintenance1): it signals once the present's queue operations have completed and the presentation engine holds what it needs, so its wait semaphores may be reused and, once all its presents have signaled, the swapchain destroyed.

terms.label: Memory heap
terms.def: A physical pool of memory the device can use, as vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties reports it: a size and whether it is device-local. On a discrete GPU typically VRAM, the share of system RAM the GPU may use, and the CPU-visible window of VRAM.

terms.label: Memory type
terms.def: One way of using a memory heap: an entry in the device's list of types that points at one heap and carries property flags (DEVICE_LOCAL, HOST_VISIBLE, ...). Every allocation comes from exactly one type.

terms.label: DEVICE_LOCAL
terms.def: A memory property flag: memory of this type is the most efficient for device access. It is set exactly when the type's heap is device-local: VRAM on a discrete GPU.

terms.label: HOST_VISIBLE
terms.def: A memory property flag: memory of this type can be mapped with vkMapMemory, which gives the CPU a pointer into it.

terms.label: HOST_COHERENT
terms.def: A memory property flag: no vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges or vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges is needed. Host writes become available in the host domain by themselves, and a queue submission makes them visible to the device.

terms.label: HOST_CACHED
terms.def: A memory property flag: the CPU accesses this memory through its caches, so reading it back is fast. Uncached host-visible memory (typically write-combined) is fine for writing and slow to read.

terms.label: LAZILY_ALLOCATED
terms.def: A memory property flag: device-only memory whose backing the implementation may provide lazily. Only images with TRANSIENT_ATTACHMENT usage may use it, never a buffer. Typical of tile-based GPUs; the course GPU has no such type.

terms.label: BAR / Resizable BAR
terms.def: The window of VRAM that the CPU can address over PCIe. Without Resizable BAR it is 256 MiB, with it the whole VRAM. Vulkan shows it as a small DEVICE_LOCAL heap with a DEVICE_LOCAL | HOST_VISIBLE type (214 MiB on the course machine, ReBAR off).

terms.label: VkDeviceMemory
terms.def: One block of memory allocated from one memory type with vkAllocateMemory. Buffers and images are bound into it at offsets.

terms.label: VkBuffer
terms.def: A linear array of bytes with a size and usage flags (vertex, index, uniform, storage, transfer source or destination). It is created without memory and becomes usable once memory is bound to it with vkBindBufferMemory.

terms.label: Memory requirements
terms.def: What a resource needs from its memory, as the driver reports it: the size to allocate, the alignment of the offset it is bound at, and memoryTypeBits, the memory types it may live in.

terms.label: memoryTypeBits
terms.def: The part of the memory requirements that lists the allowed memory types: bit i set means type i may back the resource. A type is chosen with the find-memory-type rule: the first type, in index order, that is allowed and has every wanted flag.

terms.label: Vertex buffer
terms.def: A VkBuffer with VERTEX_BUFFER usage, bound to a vertex input binding with vkCmdBindVertexBuffers: vertex attributes are fetched from it for every vertex a draw uses.

terms.label: Index buffer
terms.def: A VkBuffer of vertex indices (8, 16 or 32 bits each) bound with vkCmdBindIndexBuffer. vkCmdDrawIndexed reads it to pick the vertex for each corner of each primitive, so a vertex shared by several triangles is stored once.

terms.label: Vertex input binding
terms.def: A numbered slot of the pipeline's vertex input state that a vertex buffer is bound to, with its stride (bytes from one vertex to the next) and its rate (per vertex or per instance).

terms.label: Vertex input attribute
terms.def: One input of the vertex shader as the pipeline describes it: the shader Location it feeds, the binding it reads from, the format of the data and its offset inside one vertex.

terms.label: Staging buffer
terms.def: A buffer in host-visible memory that the CPU fills and the GPU copies from (vkCmdCopyBuffer) into device-local memory the CPU cannot map.

terms.label: Queue family ownership transfer
terms.def: Handing an EXCLUSIVE resource from one queue family to another: a release barrier on a queue of the source family and a matching acquire barrier on a queue of the destination family, ordered by an execution dependency, typically a semaphore. Without it the resource's contents are undefined for reads by the second family.

terms.label: Sub-allocation
terms.def: Placing many resources inside a few large VkDeviceMemory blocks, each at its own aligned offset, instead of one vkAllocateMemory per resource: allocations are slow, and how many may exist at once is limited.

terms.label: Linear allocator
terms.def: The simplest sub-allocator: an offset moves forward through a block, rounded up to each resource's alignment. Nothing is freed alone; the whole block is reset or freed at once. The course's Rust allocator step uses one.

terms.label: VMA (Vulkan Memory Allocator)
terms.def: AMD's open-source C/C++ library for Vulkan memory: it chooses memory types, keeps blocks per type, places resources in them with the TLSF algorithm and frees them one by one. The course's C++ allocator step uses version 3.4.0.

terms.label: bufferImageGranularity
terms.def: A device limit: linear resources (buffers, linear images) and optimal-tiling images placed next to each other in one VkDeviceMemory must not share a page of this many bytes (1024 on the course GPU).

terms.label: Uniform buffer
terms.def: A buffer that shaders read as a block of constants, the same values for every invocation of a draw; reached through a UNIFORM_BUFFER descriptor and laid out by std140 rules by default.

terms.label: Persistent mapping
terms.def: Mapping HOST_VISIBLE memory once and keeping the pointer for the program's lifetime instead of mapping and unmapping per write; vkFreeMemory unmaps it implicitly.

terms.label: std140 layout
terms.def: The block layout rule uniform buffers use by default: vectors aligned to their size (a float3 like a float4), arrays and structs aligned to 16 bytes with their size rounded up to 16.

terms.label: std430 layout
terms.def: The block layout of push constants and storage buffers: like std140 but without rounding arrays and structs to 16 bytes, so a float[2] has a stride of 4.

terms.label: Scalar block layout
terms.def: A block layout where every member is aligned only to its component size (a float3 to 4 bytes), as in a C struct; needs the scalarBlockLayout feature, which every Vulkan 1.4 device supports.

terms.label: Matrix layout
terms.def: How a matrix member lies in memory: SPIR-V's RowMajor or ColMajor decoration says whether rows or columns are stored, MatrixStride the bytes between two of them; Slang's column-major default shows up as RowMajor.

terms.label: SPIR-V reflection
terms.def: Reading a shader's interface (sets, bindings, block members, offsets) back from its SPIR-V, to check or generate the host side instead of trusting that both agree.

terms.label: Descriptor
terms.def: A small driver-defined record that tells a shader where a resource is and how to read it: for a buffer its address, offset and range; for a texture an image view and a sampler.

terms.label: Descriptor binding
terms.def: One numbered slot of a descriptor set layout: a descriptor type, a count (an array when above 1) and the shader stages that may use it; the shader names it by set and binding number.

terms.label: VkDescriptorPool
terms.def: An arena that descriptor sets are allocated from, sized up front by maxSets and a descriptor count per type; resetting or destroying it frees all its sets at once.

terms.label: VkDescriptorSet
terms.def: An instance of a descriptor set layout, allocated from a pool: its descriptors are written by vkUpdateDescriptorSets and it is bound to a set number while recording.

terms.label: Pipeline layout compatibility
terms.def: The spec's rule for when bound descriptor sets survive a pipeline switch: two pipeline layouts are compatible for set N if set layouts 0..N and the push constant ranges are identically defined.

terms.label: Sets grouped by update frequency
terms.def: A design convention, recommended in a spec note: the least frequently changing sets first (set 0 per frame, then per material, per object), so pipeline switches keep the lower sets bound.

terms.label: Push constants
terms.def: A small block of bytes recorded straight into the command buffer by vkCmdPushConstants and declared by a range of the pipeline layout: at least 128 bytes in Vulkan 1.0, at least 256 in Vulkan 1.4.

terms.label: Push descriptors
terms.def: Descriptors recorded into the command buffer by vkCmdPushDescriptorSet instead of written into an allocated set; core in Vulkan 1.4 behind the pushDescriptor feature, one such set per pipeline layout.

terms.label: Buffer device address
terms.def: The 64-bit GPU virtual address of a buffer, from vkGetBufferDeviceAddress, which shaders can dereference like a pointer; needs the feature, SHADER_DEVICE_ADDRESS usage and DEVICE_ADDRESS-allocated memory.

terms.label: PhysicalStorageBuffer
terms.def: The SPIR-V storage class of memory reached through a 64-bit address rather than a descriptor (addressing model PhysicalStorageBuffer64); loads through it state their alignment and carry no bounds.

terms.label: GPU-assisted validation
terms.def: A mode of the Khronos validation layer that instruments shaders and checks their memory and descriptor accesses while they run on the GPU; slow, and it adjusts device features for itself.

terms.label: Storage buffer
terms.def: A buffer that shaders read and may write through a STORAGE_BUFFER descriptor; std430 layout, ranges of at least 2^27 bytes, the general-purpose buffer resource.

terms.label: Descriptor indexing
terms.def: The Vulkan 1.2 features for large descriptor arrays indexed in shaders: runtime-sized arrays, non-uniform indexing, and binding flags for partially bound, variable-sized and update-after-bind bindings.

terms.label: Bindless
terms.def: A renderer design on descriptor indexing: one set holding the descriptors of all resources, bound once, with each draw or instance passing only an index into it.

terms.label: Variable descriptor count
terms.def: A binding flag: the layout's descriptorCount is an upper bound and each set gets its own length at allocation; allowed only on the highest-numbered binding.

terms.label: Partially bound
terms.def: A binding flag: descriptors that no invocation actually accesses (not dynamically used) may stay unwritten; without it every statically used descriptor must be valid.

terms.label: Update after bind
terms.def: Binding flags that relax when a set may change: UPDATE_AFTER_BIND between bind and submit (the GPU sees the new descriptors), UPDATE_UNUSED_WHILE_PENDING for elements a pending command buffer does not use.

terms.label: Dynamically uniform
terms.def: A value that is the same for every invocation of an invocation group, which for a vertex shader is all invocations of one draw command; an instance index is not.

terms.label: Non-uniform indexing
terms.def: Indexing a descriptor array with a value that differs between invocations: needs the feature and SPIR-V capability, and the NonUniform decoration on the operand of the access itself.

terms.label: Subgroup
terms.def: A group of shader invocations scheduled together on one shader core that can share data and synchronize efficiently, 32 on the course GPU (a warp on NVIDIA, a wave on AMD); Vulkan does not promise they run in lockstep (NVIDIA Volta and later schedule threads independently), and hardware may keep values shared by the whole subgroup in scalar registers.
